Sriram Kartik sweeps 10 awards including the ‘Best Junior contestant’ across Carnatic vocal and mrudangam; prizes presented by eminent Vidwan Sikkil Gurucharan on 23 Aug 2026 in MumbaiA fifteen-year-old from Powai has won ten awards at the Music Competition 2026 conducted by Sri Shanmukhananda Bharatiya Sangeetha Vidyalaya and Natya Vidyalaya, competing in both Carnatic vocal and mrudangam.Sriram Kartik, a Class X IGCSE student at Podar International School, received the awards at the prize distribution ceremony held on Sunday (Aug 23, 2026) on the occasion of Shanmukhananda's Carnataka Sangeetha Pon Mazhai Thiruvizha, at the Sri Shanmukhananda Fine Arts and Sangeetha Sabha in Matunga. The prizes were presented by Shanmukha Sangeetha Shiromani Vidwan Shri Sikkil Gurucharan, the eminent Carnatic vocalist, who presided over the ceremony.Vidwan Sikkil C Gurucharan is a leading Indian Carnatic classical vocalist and youth ambassador for the art form. A singer born into a family of flautists, and grandson of Sikkil Kunjumani, the elder of the Sikkil Sisters, he trained under B Krishnamurthy and Vaigal S. Gnanaskandan, himself a disciple of Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer and gave his first concert at The Music Academy, Chennai at the age of twelve. Recipient of the Kalaimamani award from the Tamil Nadu government in 2020, Sikkil C Gurucharan has been featured by India Today as one of the 35 Game Changers Under 35 in India.Sriram Kartik won 9 individual prizes — five first prizes, three seconds and one third. He was also awarded a cash prize for being the Best Junior contestant winning the maximum number of prizes in the 10-to-15 years age category.The competition, the Vidyalaya's 70th annual, was held on February 7 and 8 across Carnatic vocal, violin, veena, mrudangam, Hindustani vocal, sitar and tabla. It drew more than 300 participants from across India and overseas, contesting in three age groups: 10 to 15, 16 to 28, and 29 and above.Sriram's two mrudangam prizes came in the only two categories open to his age group — a first for tani avartanam in roopakam and misra chapu talams, and a second for adi talam with five jathi mohras, awarded under the TS Nandakumar's Percussive Arts Centre Endowment and the Guru TS Nandakumar Endowment respectively.His seven vocal prizes spanned first places in compositions of the Trinity, varnams, Purandaradasa kritis; the Silver Lamp Prize for keertanams and kritis; second places in Subramania Bharatiyar compositions and Tamizh compositions; and a third in GNB kritis.Every prize at Shanmukhananda is attached to an endowment instituted in the name of an artist, a patron or an institution. He won awards under the following endowments namely - GNB Endowment, the Kalki Memorial, the Dr S Pinakapani Endowment, the BVS Iyengar Memorial and the Lakshmi Gopalakrishna Memorial. The Best Junior award came under the Smt. Parvathy Subramaniam Endowment and S Ramakrishnan Memorial.Sriram began learning the mrudangam at the age of five, under Acharya Ratna Vidwan Mumbai Shri Shankaranarayanan at Powai Fine Arts. A decade on, he has kept at it through the school years in which most students of classical music quietly stop — the age at which coaching classes, board examinations and the ordinary pull of everything else tend to close the practice room door for good.Sustaining it alongside school is the part a prize list does not show. Practice sessions run two and a half to three hours. Nine vocal categories at 5-6 compositions a piece meant something close to 45-50 pieces in which he participated of which he won prizes across seven categories, readied to a standard that would survive a judging panel, with two percussion categories besides.He now receives higher tutelage in mrudangam from Padma Vibhushan and Sangeet Natak Academi Awardee Vidwan Dr Umayalpuram K Sivaraman, and trains in Carnatic vocal music under Acharya Ratnakara Vidwan Sherthalai Dr KN Renganatha Sharma and Vidushi Dr Mohana Sharma. He holds a CCRT Scholarship for Mrudangam from the ministry of culture, and presented his mrudangam arangetram in June last year, the day after his fourteenth birthday.
Article Summary: Sriram kartik received awards at prize distribution ceremony held on sunday (aug 23, 2026) on the occasion of shanmukhananda's carnataka sangeetha pon mazhai thiruvizha. The competition drew more than 300 participants from across india and overseas, contesting in three age groups: 10 to 15, 16 to 28, and 29 and above.

Article Title: Why is Michael Jordan bidding farewell to his lucrative $40 million-a-year deal? All about the NBA upset
Article Text:

Why Michael Jordan won't return for NBC's $40 million NBA deal

Michael Jordan reportedly not returning to NBC's NBA coverage

Why Michael Jordan is not coming back to NBC

Backlash puts NBC's marquee hire in question

There will not be any debate around the fact that the end of Michael Jordan ’s NBC role as an analyst is going to be a major upset for the fans worldwide. Regardless, MJ is reportedly not coming back to the role. While the contract was quite lucrative with a whopping $40 million a year attached to the deal, we all need to question, does Jordan need more money? For context, Jordan is the wealthiest athlete in the world with over a staggering $4.3 billion net worth to his name, according to Forbes. But what’s actually going on and what’s the real reason behind Jordan’s reported decision.Michael Jordan appears to be done with NBC. Multiple reports this week point to the NBA legend skipping a second season with the network, ending a run that once looked like the year's biggest broadcasting coup.The move comes after Jordan signed on last year for a reported $40 million a year as a special contributor to NBC's NBA coverage. What changed between that splashy announcement and now is a story of high expectations, thin output, and a legend who has never liked talking much anyway.According to Front Office Sports, Jordan is unlikely to be part of NBC's basketball coverage for the 2026-27 season. The Daily Mail reached out to NBC for comment and did not hear back.Jordan's addition to the network last May was billed as a coup, since he had barely appeared on camera since The Last Dance aired in 2020. Fans expected regular appearances and sharp analysis throughout the season. Instead, Jordan sat down with host Mike Tirico just once. The single conversation got split into five segments and rolled out across several weeks of the campaign, which left part of the audience unimpressed.Some fans and analysts felt shortchanged. They wanted more from a name as big as Jordan's, and five scattered clips over months did not match the buildup.Tirico pushed back hard against the criticism. He pointed out that Jordan has never been much of a talker, and noted Jordan's ownership stake in the Charlotte Hornets and his role at Jordan Brand as reasons his time is stretched thin. According to Tirico, Jordan wanted to focus specifically on where he sees the state of the league right now, not run through a long list of topics.Jordan reportedly used part of that conversation to question whether today's highest paid stars love the game as much as his generation did. Tirico defended the format anyway: "Was it better than not hearing from Michael Jordan? You're damn right it was."He added that hearing Jordan's take as the greatest player of all time carries a weight that a hundred hot takes about a single injury never will.Not everyone bought the defense. Charles Barkley, never shy with an opinion, put it plainly: "It's a bad look for NBC." The comment stuck, and it captured a frustration that had been building since the deal was first announced.Front Office Sports did not report an official reason behind the expected exit. That silence leaves room for speculation about whether the split was Jordan's call, the network's, or something both sides worked out quietly and would rather not detail.
Article Summary: Michael jordan is reportedly skipping a second season with nbc's nba coverage. The move comes after jordan signed on last year for a reported $40 million a year as a special contributor. Jordan's addition to the network last may was billed as a coup since he had barely appeared on camera since the last dance aired in 2020.

UAE batter Asif Khan has been banned for 15 months after testing positive for a banned anabolic steroid during an out-of-competition doping test conducted last year.Asif tested positive for a metabolite of mesterolone in a sample collected on September 8, 2025. Mesterolone is an anabolic steroid used to increase testosterone levels.The 36-year-old admitted to violating Article 2.1 of the ICC Anti-Doping Code and accepted the sanction through a Case Resolution Agreement with the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and the International Cricket Council (ICC)."The 36-year-old admitted to a violation of Article 2.1 of the ICC Anti-Doping Code and accepted the sanction through a Case Resolution Agreement with the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and the International Cricket Council (ICC)," read a statement from cricket's world governing body.The ban has been backdated to September 8, 2025 and will run until December 7, 2026. Asif will be allowed to resume training with a team or use the facilities of a club or other ICC Member organisation from October 8, but he will only be eligible to return to competitive cricket from December 8."Asif will be permitted to return to training with a team or use the facilities of a club or other ICC Member organisation from October 8, but will only be eligible to return to competitive cricket from December 8," the ICC statement said.The ICC has also disqualified Asif's individual results from September 8, 2025 until the start of his provisional suspension on December 29, 2025."This includes all resulting consequences, such as the loss of any medals, points, prize money or prizes."Asif, who was born in Pakistan and moved to the UAE in 2017, has represented the UAE in 38 ODIs and 56 T20 Internationals since making his international debut in 2022.Before moving to the UAE, the right-handed batter played 32 first-class matches in Pakistan's domestic cricket.

After two seasons with the Toronto Maple Leafs organization, Alex Nylander is heading to the Calgary Flames on a professional tryout at training camp. The move gives the 28-year-old forward another shot at fighting for an NHL roster spot after limited action at the highest level in Toronto.This follows Nylander having one of his better recent seasons in the AHL with the Toronto Marlies. He played a part in helping the Marlies to a Calder Cup win, but his NHL opportunities remained scarce.The pro tryout provides Alex Nylander another chance to vie for NHL employment, and it also means he’s in the Calgary Flames’ training-camp plans.Nylander had 24 goals, 29 assists and 53 points in 65 regular-season games with the Toronto Marlies in the 2025-26 AHL season. He scored six goals and added seven points in 24 playoff games as Toronto claimed the Calder Cup.That outing is why Nylander remains an intriguing depth option even with an inconsistent NHL career. The Buffalo Sabres selected him eighth overall in the 2016 NHL Draft, but he has recorded 49 points in 126 NHL games.Nylander most recently played in the NHL in 2024-25 with the Toronto Maple Leafs, where he appeared in five games and did not record a point.Most of his recent production has been at the AHL level, though.His move to Calgary is thus a chance to reboot his NHL career. But there’s no guarantee of an NHL contract or a spot on the roster with the PTO. Nylander will have to impress the Calgary Flames in training camp and preseason.The Calgary Flames offer Nylander a new environment, though a permanent NHL spot is still up for grabs. His strong AHL production makes a strong case for another opportunity, while his career NHL numbers explain why the Flames will likely be cautious with him.Nylander’s immediate goal is simple: take his scoring success with the Toronto Marlies and parlay it into an NHL opportunity with the Calgary Flames. Alex Nylander is exiting the Toronto Maple Leafs organization after two seasons, signing a professional tryout with the Calgary Flames, and the 28-year-old forward is coming off a solid 2025-26 AHL season with the Toronto Marlies, helping them win the Calder Cup. Nylander could get another chance to play in the NHL in Calgary.The move gives Nylander a fresh opportunity after limited NHL action in Toronto. He recorded 24 goals and 53 points in 65 AHL games last season before adding seven points during the Marlies’ championship run. His NHL experience includes stops with several teams, making Calgary another important chance to revive his career.

An entire city.And then you go out and pose like you’re just watching TV, or reportedly make an X user feel like, “MF is eye f*cking me through the phone.” That’s a whole other universe of a story.Maybe it was fine when it was limited to his colorful nail polish - not just black, goth-like, or one painted nail, but all colorful nails. Tom Aspinall is still the UFC heavyweight champion, but his long break from the Octagon has created a question nobody really wanted hanging over the division: Is he actually leaving? That question was picked up after his boxing coach, Stipe Drvis, claimed Aspinall wanted out of the UFC. The champion shut that down himself, saying the reports were wrong. His message was pretty direct, and it also gave fans one useful detail: talks with the UFC are still happening. Here’s the full statement from him and what he wanted to say to his fans and the UFC community.After Drvis made the claim about his future, Aspinall posted a statement on X to address it directly. He wrote,He also stressed that he had never said that in an interview and said comments attributed to other people wereThe champion then added that his team is speaking with the UFC every day. His own statement points to ongoing discussions about what comes next.For now, that leaves the supposed exit claim resting against Aspinall’s own words. He has publicly denied wanting to leave, while his absence continues to keep questions around his next fight alive.The confusion mostly comes from how long Aspinall has been away. His last appearance was at UFC 321 in October 2025, where his fight with Ciryl Gane ended as a no-contest after an eye poke left him unable to continue. Put those pieces together, and speculation about a possible UFC exit started making more sense to some people. Gane won the interim UFC heavyweight title after defeating Alex Pereira at UFC Freedom 250 in June. That result set up a rematch with Aspinall, this time as a heavyweight title unification bout.So, once Aspinall is ready to return, Gane is the man waiting on the other side. The only real uncertainty is the date. Article Title: Sonal Dinusha joins elite list of legends with remarkable run against India
Article Text:

Sonal Dinusha continued his impressive run against India by registering his fourth consecutive fifty-plus score in Test cricket on Thursday, putting his name alongside some of the game's most celebrated batters.The Sri Lankan left-hander reached the landmark during the final day of the second Test in Colombo, where his resilient innings helped the hosts keep their hopes of saving the match alive. Dinusha's latest half-century came after he had already produced three substantial scores across the two-Test series.𝟓𝟎-𝐩𝐥𝐮𝐬 𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐢𝐧 𝐟𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐢𝐧𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐭 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚Douglas Jardine (ENG, 1932-1934)Everton Weekes (WI, 1948)Clyde Walcott (WI, 1948)Ken Barrington (ENG, 1959)Sonal Dinusha (SL, 2026)Dinusha began the series with a century and an 84 in the first Test. He then followed those efforts with 103 in the first innings of the second Test before completing another fifty-plus score in the second innings.The consistency has placed him in several notable statistical lists.Dinusha has become only the third Sri Lankan batter to record fifty-plus scores in all four innings of a two-Test series. He joins Kumar Sangakkara and Dimuth Karunaratne in achieving the feat.Sangakkara accomplished it against Bangladesh at home in 2013 and against England in England in 2014, while Karunaratne achieved the feat against South Africa at home in 2018.Dinusha's achievement against India is even rarer. He is only the second batter to score fifty-plus in each of his first four Test innings against India.The only previous batter to achieve that feat was Zimbabwe great Andy Flower during Zimbabwe's tour of India in 2000. Flower's scores across the four innings were 183*, 70, 55 and 232*.Dinusha has also entered another exclusive list involving India. He is the fifth batter to score fifty-plus in each of his first four Test innings against the country.England's Douglas Jardine achieved the feat between 1932 and 1934, while West Indies legends Everton Weekes and Clyde Walcott did so in 1948. England's Ken Barrington followed in 1959.Dinusha's latest contribution came at a crucial stage for Sri Lanka. His half-century, combined with a century partnership with Keshara Nuwantha, allowed the hosts to negotiate the first session of the final day without losing a wicket and maintain their hopes of securing a draw.
Article Summary: Sonal dinusha scored his fourth consecutive fifty-plus score in test cricket. The sri lankan left-hander reached the landmark during the final day of the second test in colombo. Dinusha's latest half-century came after he had already produced three substantial scores across the two-test series.

Article Title: Women's Hockey World Cup: India look to sign off with Germany test
Article Text:
Indian women’s hockey team

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Indian women’s hockey team will look to end their World Cup campaign on a high when they face Germany in the fifth-sixth place classification match at Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen on Thursday.Having played five matches so far, India have won one, drawn three and lost only once — against hosts Netherlands. It has been an impressive campaign for a team that looked out of sorts last year, and coach Sjoerd Marijne has been more than pleased with the progress his wards have made.“I told the girls, ‘If I had told you six months ago that we would play a quarterfinal against Australia at the World Cup and draw 0-0, would you have believed it?’ I don’t think, considering the position they were in six months ago, they would have believed it,” said Marijne in a video released by Hockey India.Indeed, India have produced a fascinating campaign, with almost everyone contributing at different stages. The only glaring gap has been their inability to convert chances into goals consistently — something that eventually ended their hopes of reaching the semifinals.“We have really made good progress, and it’s not easy to score goals against these teams. The basis of our game is our defence, and we do that really well,” Marijne said.Apart from their games against China and South Africa, India failed to score against England, Netherlands and Australia. It was not for a lack of opportunities, but rather their inability to make those chances count when it mattered most.That will once again be put to the test against Germany, coached by a familiar face in former India head coach Janneke Schopman.Germany, too, have been through a transition since the Paris Olympics and could not make the semifinals after losing their two crucial matches against Argentina and Belgium. They did, however, win three matches across the two rounds, while scoring 13 goals in the process.Their ability to find the net has been one of their biggest positives, but breaking down India’s defence could prove a different challenge.Schopman knows this Indian team well from her time as their head coach and is likely to have plenty of insight into how to exploit their weaknesses. However, India have shown they can be extremely difficult to break down when they get their defensive structure right.England had 20 shots on goal and 12 penalty corners in their 0-0 draw with India, while Australia managed 13 shots and five penalty corners in India's last game. Neither could find a way past the Indian defence.Speaking about the Australia match, Marijne said, “We evaluated the game with the team, and sometimes these things happen in a process. Sometimes you take a step back to make two steps forward. But again, we didn’t lose; we just didn’t win.”India may not be playing for a medal, but Thursday’s game offers them one final opportunity to underline the progress they have made at the World Cup.A strong finish against Germany would also give the team valuable confidence heading into the Asian Games, where a gold medal would bring with it a direct qualification spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Article Summary: India face germany in the fifth-sixth place classification match at wagener hockey stadium in amstelveen on thursday. India have won one, drawn three and lost only once — against hosts netherlands. Coach sjoerd marijne has been more than pleased with the progress his wards have made.

Article Title: Magnus Carlsen has a lot to teach, he’s one of the best, says Divya Deshmukh

Divya Deshmukh will make her Global Chess League debut with defending champions Alpine APL Pipers, led by world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen

Women’s World Cup winner Divya Deshmukh will make her Global Chess League (GCL) debut with defending champions Alpine APL Pipers, led by world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen . With a lineup featuring the positional precision of Anish Giri and Vidit Gujrathi, the experience of Koneru Humpy and reigning world rapid champion Volodar Murzin, the addition of 20-year-old Divya makes Pipers one of the strongest contenders in the fourth season of the GCL.Divya is excited to make her debut alongside a well-balanced team. Speaking with, Divya said, “I am very excited that Alpine Pipers chose me and it was the team that I was secretly hoping I would get selected in. So it was a very happy moment for me when I found out that they took me. And I am looking forward to it. I am especially happy about Murzin because we also share a team in World Rapid, Blitz and of course he’s very good.”Divya is also looking forward to learning some tricks from World No. 1 Carlsen, the team leader. “It’s my first time being a teammate with Carlsen. We’ve met before but haven’t interacted much. Now that I’m a teammate, it’s a nice opportunity to learn some things from him. He has a lot to teach and he’s one of the best,” she said.With India on the verge of getting its 100th Grandmaster, Divya is excited. “I don’t know who’s in the running.I’m hoping that there will be more female GMs from India. Right now, I’m hoping that a woman becomes India’s 100th GM.”On adapting with teammates who are also her opponents, Divya said, “It’s not difficult to adapt because I’ve played against them. It feels nice that we will be playing on the same team. And also in the Olympiad, we’ll be playing on the same team. So we’ll be teammates for a month.”On being the youngest Arjuna Awardee, Divya said, “After a shaky year, it was nice to win the Arjuna Award. I just hope to attend the ceremony. I’m hoping it’ll be held in Dec, because in Oct I’ll be representing India and playing GCL in Sept.”Asked about the flexibility of pairings in GCL where a team comprises mixed genders, Divya said, “It’s fun to mix things around. So maybe something like we can have a board order on. Let’s say something like we play on any board and opposite team can do the same. So we can never know the pairing.It would be quite chaotic, but it would be fun.”At her debut appearance in the 2026 Cairns Cup in St Louis, USA, recently, Divya had a strong start but finished tied fifth to seventh. On her overall performance, she said, “It was very average, I would say. I had a good tournament till I lost to Tan (Zhongyi), which was an unfortunate game because I was pressing the whole time and then did not manage my time well and went down on time and ended up making a mistake. Overall the games that I played were actually very good. Since I didn’t feel any pressure I played very good chess.”

Anaya Bangar's return to competitive cricket now has a potential timeline, with March 2027 set as the key date in her bid to pursue elite women's cricket in Australia and potentially earn a route into the Women's Big Bash League.The former Mumbai U-19 cricketer has been cleared by Cricket Australia to play community cricket and has been given a pathway to pursue elite women's cricket, subject to the governing body's eligibility requirements.Bangar, the daughter of former India cricketer and ex-India batting coach Sanjay Bangar , stressed that the clearance does not amount to selection for the WBBL or automatic entry into elite cricket. Instead, it gives her an opportunity to work towards that level.“I am preparing to return to women’s cricket in Australia with the aim of pursuing elite cricket from March 2027,” the 25-year-old said. “This has not been an automatic or an informal process. Cricket Australia has a framework designed to balance fairness, competitive integrity, and inclusion in women’s sport, and my case has been considered through that framework.”Bangar said she understands that she will have to earn any opportunity that comes her way.“Cricket Australia has given me a pathway, which does not mean that I have been given a place in a team. I still have to train, compete, perform and earn that opportunity,” she said.Bangar's immediate plan is to find a club and play community cricket in Australia as she works towards a return to the competitive game. Her participation in elite competitions, including the WBBL, will depend on Cricket Australia's Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy.Under the policy, a player's serum testosterone concentration must remain below 10 nmol/L for at least 12 months to qualify for elite cricket.Bangar's eligibility will be assessed from March 2027, including through a required blood test.“My understanding from Cricket Australia's clearance is that my eligibility for elite women's cricket from March 2027 remains subject to the applicable policy requirements, including a blood test assessment at the same time. If that March 2027 test confirms that I continue to meet the required testosterone criteria, I will be eligible to pursue selection for elite women’s cricket, including the Women’s Big Bash League pathway,” Bangar said.Meeting those requirements would allow Bangar to seek selection, but would not guarantee her a place in an elite team.“I don’t expect my history or my identity to earn me a place on a cricket team. I want my cricket to earn me a place on a cricket team,” she said.Bangar had earlier sought clarity from the Board of Control for Cricket in India ( BCCI ) over whether transgender athletes could compete in women's cricket in India. She said she received no response to a letter submitted last year.She subsequently approached Cricket Australia in June this year.According to Bangar, Cricket Australia assessed her medical records, blood tests, documents relating to her surgeries and a research report from Manchester Metropolitan University's Institute of Sport before reaching its decision.“After I published my athlete testing report and everything else, BCCI stayed quiet about it. Whereas Cricket Australia actually read my report, went through all my medical history and had a proper team assessing my case,” Bangar said.“I approached Cricket Australia and they gave me clearance to play in terms of fairness and inclusivity.”Bangar is now looking for a club in Australia, with community cricket set to be the first step in her attempt to rebuild her playing career and eventually pursue an opportunity in elite women's cricket.

Article Title: What’s going on with Kyle Singler? 6-foot-8 ex-Thunder star posts disturbing video about Coach K

Kyle Singler is at the center of a troubling story after the former Duke standout posted a string of rambling Instagram videos this week, aiming pointed accusations at his old college coach, Mike Krzyzewski. The clips show him pacing through what looks like an empty house, insisting people are trying to hurt him and take his money.It's a jarring turn for a guy once known for hitting big shots on college basketball's biggest stage. Now the questions aren't about his jumper. They're about his safety.The videos surfaced on Tuesday night, and they don't look good. Kyle Singler, 38, wanders from room to room, appears to be agitated, describing a life that sounds nothing like the one he built during his NBA years. He says his power has been shut off. He says his house has been broken into. He says money is being drained from accounts he can barely track anymore.None of that has been independently verified. But the pattern is familiar to anyone who followed his last public flare-up. Back in November 2024, Singler posted something similar, telling followers he feared for his life every single day. This week's videos pick up roughly where that one left off, only louder and more disjointed.There's also history sitting underneath all of this. Singler was arrested in Oklahoma last October after his girlfriend told police he grabbed her by the head and shoved her to the ground during an argument at an Airbnb, with their child present. He posted bond on a misdemeanor charge and the case has largely stayed out of headlines since, until now.Singler didn't just vent about strangers or unnamed enemies. He went after Krzyzewski directly, the coach who guided him to a national title in 2010 and later called him one of the most complete players he'd ever developed.Singler claims he reached out for help and got nothing back. "Coach K has set me up, man," he said in one clip, adding that Krzyzewski had "fully dismissed" his messages.“You guys are cutting my power off, breaking into my house, stealing money, ruining my life. I reached out to Coach K and all he did was sit me on the bench. Thanks, man. Is that what we're doing at that school, sitting people down, teaching them up? Cool beans, man.Coach, where you at? Help a brother out. Thought we were on the same team, man," Singler shared.He described feeling abandoned by the program he once helped define, at one point comparing his situation to being benched, as though the man who shaped his career had simply stopped answering the phone.It's worth remembering where Singler came from. He was the engine of Duke's 2010 championship run, earned Most Outstanding Player honors in that tournament, and went on to play seven NBA seasons split between Detroit and Oklahoma City after going 33rd overall in 2011. He pulled in more than $22 million over his career, most of it from a contract extension with the Thunder.

Singler claims he reached out for help and got nothing back from his old coach, mike krzyzewski.

Article Title: After 75 years the Pro Bowl is dead: Here's what replaces the game nobody wanted to watch
Article Text:
NFL ends the Pro Bowl game after 75 years (Via X)

Why did the NFL cancel the Pro Bowl game?

What happens to the Pro Bowl now that the game is gone?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The NFL officially ended the Pro Bowl game on Wednesday, closing out a 75-year tradition that had slowly lost the plot. The league announced at its owners meeting in Atlanta that no game will be played after this season. Players selected as Pro Bowlers will still receive the honor and gather in Los Angeles for a celebration, but the actual football game is gone. This is not a pause. The NFL is not regrouping. It is a full stop on what had become the most skippable event on the sports calendar.The honest answer is that the players stopped caring, and the league finally admitted it out loud. NFL executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent spoke directly with more than a dozen star players this summer, and what he heard was consistent. They did not want competitive football after the playoffs ended. Vincent put it plainly at the owners meeting: "You come off the championship games and the viewers see the physicality of the game and you try to replicate that. Frankly, it just doesn't sit well. This isn't a good representation."That admission matters more than it might seem. For years the NFL kept pushing the format, hoping a tweak would fix the problem.The game moved out of Honolulu, the home it had for decades. In 2023 the league switched entirely to flag football, hoping the casual format would generate energy. It did not. Ratings stayed soft. Players showed up out of obligation, not excitement. Nobody was fooled.Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's executive vice president overseeing events, framed the decision with uncommon directness. "It's OK to be the first league to walk away from a competitive all-star game," he said in Atlanta. That line will not make headlines for its poetry, but it signals something real: the NFL is no longer interested in defending a product it cannot fix.The title survives. The game does not. The NFL confirmed that 88 players will still earn Pro Bowl recognition after this season and be honored at an event in Los Angeles. Several flag football exhibitions will take place around that time, though they will serve as entertainment rather than competition. The core distinction, being named one of the best at your position in the NFL, stays intact.The league also eliminated replacement selections going forward. In the past, injured players or Super Bowl participants were swapped out for alternates, which diluted the honor. Cleveland Browns rookie quarterback Shedeur Sanders made the Pro Bowl this year as a replacement. Under the new structure, that category is gone. If a player earns it, they earn it outright.O'Reilly explained the thinking behind the restructured honor: "The Pro Bowl has always been about recognizing the players who distinguish themselves as the very best in the NFL. A Pro Bowl selection will return to its original purpose, honoring the best of the best. We want that distinction to carry even greater meaning for the players, their families, their clubs and our fans."The voting process stays the same: an equal split between players, coaches, and fans. What changes is the weight behind it. Without a game to water things down, a Pro Bowl selection becomes a cleaner acknowledgment of a great season rather than a footnote to an event most people forgot was happening.
Article Summary: Nfl ends the pro bowl game after 75 years. The league announced at its owners meeting in atlanta that no game will be played after this season. Players selected as pro bowlers will still receive the honor and gather in los angeles for a celebration, but the actual football game is gone.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “I almost died after giving birth to my daughter.” - How Serena Williams turned life-threatening motherhood and family strength into sporting resilience
Article Text:
Serena Williams makes Cincinnati return with Venus after ‘emotional’ family moment with daughters Olympia and Adira

How did Serena Williams almost die after giving birth to Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr.

How did Alexis Ohanian support Serena Williams during her recovery

How did Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. become Serena Williams’ motivation

Why did Serena Williams choose family when she stepped away from tennis

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Serena Williams’ story of motherhood is also a story of survival. In 2017, the tennis star won the Australian Open while eight weeks pregnant, then nearly died after giving birth to her daughter, Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. An emergency C-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight Grand Slam finals. Her daughter Olympia became an important part of that journey. Years later, Serena chose to step away from singles tennis to focus on her family, while continuing to build her life beyond the court.Serena’s pregnancy had gone well, but the birth of Olympia on September 1, 2017, quickly became dangerous. Olympia was delivered by emergency C-section after her heart rate dropped sharply during contractions. The surgery itself went well, and Serena was able to hold her daughter. The serious problems started about a day later.Serena suddenly had trouble breathing. Because she had a history of blood clots, she suspected she was having another pulmonary embolism, a condition in which a blood clot blocks blood flow in the lungs.She asked for a CT scan and blood thinner treatment. Doctors later found several small clots in her lungs.The treatment then caused another problem. Serena’s intense coughing made her C-section wound open. Doctors found a large hematoma, or a collection of blood, in her abdomen. She needed more surgery and another procedure to help stop future clots from reaching her lungs. After leaving the hospital, Serena spent the first six weeks of motherhood in bed and had difficulty even walking.Serena later described the experience in a CNN opinion piece, making clear just how close she believed she had come to losing her life.“I almost died after giving birth to my daughter, Olympia. Yet I consider myself fortunate… When I finally made it home to my family, with only days left in my recovery, I felt a deep sense of gratitude just to hold my baby girl in my arms.”The CNN piece was also about the wider problem of maternal health and the need for better access to care. Serena credited the doctors and nurses who treated her with helping save her life.For Serena, recovering from childbirth was not only about getting her body strong enough to play tennis again. She was also learning how to care for a newborn while she was unable to move normally.Her husband, Alexis Ohanian, was there during that difficult period. In Serena’s 2018 Vogue interview, Ohanian spoke about how hard it was to watch his wife struggle while he could not take away what she was going through. Serena also described how difficult those first weeks were as a new mother.That made her return to tennis different from any comeback she had made before. She was not simply trying to get her ranking back. She was trying to find a way to be a professional athlete and a mother at the same time.When Serena returned to competition, she faced another challenge. After her long break, she had fallen far down the rankings and had to work her way back into major events. She eventually reached the 2018 Wimbledon final, less than a year after giving birth.Olympia was born into a world where her mother was already one of the biggest names in tennis. But after the difficult birth, motherhood gave Serena a different reason to keep going.During her return, Serena spoke openly about the emotional side of being a mother and an athlete. Her run to the Wimbledon final in 2018 became one of the clearest signs that she could still compete at the highest level after everything her body had gone through.After the Wimbledon final, Serena also dedicated her performance to mothers watching her. She had lost to Angelique Kerber, but the result did not take away from what she had achieved by reaching the final so soon after giving birth.“Olympia, does mama look good out here? You’re the reason I’m here, you’re my motivation. To all the moms out there, I was playing for you today. It’s okay to have hard days, but we keep fighting.”That message summed up what her comeback had come to mean. Serena was not hiding the difficult parts of motherhood. She was showing that returning to work after having a child can involve fear, setbacks and days when the body simply does not cooperate.Her run did not stop at Wimbledon. Serena reached four straight Grand Slam singles finals after becoming a mother: Wimbledon and the US Open in 2018, followed by the Australian Open and Wimbledon in 2019. She did not win those finals, but reaching them showed how quickly she had returned to the top of the sport.By 2022, Serena was ready for another major change. She did not want to call it retirement. In her Vogue essay announcing her decision to move away from professional tennis, she called it an “evolution.”Her decision was closely tied to her family. Serena wrote about Olympia’s wish to become a big sister and her own desire to have another child. At the same time, she wanted to give more attention to Serena Ventures and the other parts of her life that had grown alongside her tennis career.“I have never liked the word retirement… Maybe the best word to describe what I’m up to is evolution. I’m here to tell you that I’m evolving away from tennis, toward other things that are important to me… My daughter wants to be a big sister, and I want to be there for my family.”Vogue published Serena’s essay in August 2022, ahead of what she described as her final US Open. She later welcomed her second daughter, Adira River Ohanian, with Alexis Ohanian in August 2023.Serena’s tennis story has since taken another unexpected turn. In 2026, she returned to competitive tennis, making her comeback first in doubles and later joining Carlos Alcaraz for the US Open mixed doubles event. That means her relationship with the sport is still evolving, even after she stepped away from singles competition in 2022.Her motherhood journey remains one of the most personal parts of that story. Serena went from a frightening medical crisis after Olympia’s birth to competing in Grand Slam finals again. She then made a choice to put family at the centre of her next chapter. For Serena, strength was not only about winning another match. It was also about surviving, recovering and finding a new reason to keep moving forward.
Article Summary: Serena williams almost died after giving birth to her daughter, alexis olympia ohanian jr. an emergency c-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight grand slam finals.

Article Title: "I’ve sacrificed a lot": Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' director Kelli Finglass confronts the possibility of walking away from the America's Sweetheart
Article Text:
America’s Sweethearts

Kelli Finglass on Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and social media criticism

Kelli Finglass reveals her future with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders

For Kelli Finglass , leading the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has never been only about flawless routines and game-day glamour. Her role has placed her at the center of auditions, tough decisions, television scrutiny and the changing pressures faced by young performers. As Netflix’sreturns for season three, Finglass is reflecting on criticism, motherhood, vulnerability and the possibility of eventually stepping away.Kelli Finglass knows exactly what it takes to become a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader because she once stood where the dancers now stand. She performed for the Cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. Her career has since become closely tied to the evolution of the organization on television.The Netflix series has brought unprecedented attention to the cheerleaders, but that visibility has a downside. Social media criticism can follow the women beyond the dance studio, something Finglass says she has seen affect members of the team.She does not make a habit of reading online comments herself. Still, she understands the emotional weight they can carry.“The words of people, while they can be very, very uplifting...Like in my personal case with my skin cancer journey, the people that reached out to me were extremely supportive," she said in an interview with Vanity Fair."Words can hurt and they can also heal. I’m trusting humanity to help figure this one out because it’s a much bigger thing than I can solve. But the girls being busy and focused and supportive of each other is where our strength will remain.”That outlook reflects a major lesson Finglass has learned through years of television. The cheerleaders do not need to appear perfect all the time.Kelli Finglass has also reconsidered what leadership means as she has grown older. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances.Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.“I spent practically my whole career trying to create flawless performances, and what we’ve learned through TV is that vulnerability is actually more attractive. People love when they can relate to somebody, and that’s been an unexpected “aha” for me—for these girls to not project perfection, but rather be honest about their victories and honest about their struggles, has, I hope, given viewers something to find hope in and find something they can relate to.”..Now entering her 35th season with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, retirement is no longer an impossible thought. Finglass says her family could ultimately influence that decision, especially as she looks toward becoming a grandmother someday.“I have, but we’re so busy, we don’t have time to think about anything except the next hour. It would be a personal decision. I’ve sacrificed a lot of time with my family. My daughter is married, my son is in a relationship, and when I ever get the honor to be a grandma…I want that time if and when I have grandchildren. That would definitely give me a heartfelt reason to go to a new chapter.”For now, Finglass remains focused on the next generation. Her story has become intertwined with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, but her lasting message may be simpler: perfection is impressive, while vulnerability can be powerful.
Article Summary: Kelli finglass performed for the cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances. Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.

Article Title: Prasidh Krishna reveals his definition of aggression: 'It's about what I'm doing'
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Every fast bowler has his own way of showing aggression. Some try to unsettle batters with eye contact, some stay calm, others rely on yorkers, constant appeals or words. India pacer Prasidh Krishna has a different approach - he believes his aggression is best shown through his bowling.Krishna credited disciplined bowling, strong fielding and an attacking mindset for India’s early success against Sri Lanka. The hosts were reduced to 8/2 before bad light ended Day Two of the second Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground on Monday. India had declared on 503/9 after centuries from Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel.The bowlers had only a short window to work with, but Krishna made it count, picking up a wicket with just his second delivery of the second over.Krishna said aggression is not necessarily about showing emotion or getting into a verbal battle with the opposition.“Yeah, I would like to say so. I mean, aggression can come out in different ways, and for me it is about what I'm doing when I'm bowling. It's very easy for people to get away or be distracted by what's happening in the pitch.There's too much happening, there's not too much happening, but I think the focus is still to come in and bowl those areas with full effort,” Krishna told the broadcasters before the start of Day 3’s play.Krishna bowled back of a length outside off and found enough movement from the surface to trouble Lahiru Udara. The Sri Lankan opener edged towards gully, where Yashasvi Jaiswal completed an excellent diving catch to dismiss him for one.Krishna said the wicket was a result of both the conditions and Jaiswal’s fielding effort.“Yeah, I think it was, there’s something in the pitch, of course. Maybe stopped a little bit. There was a bit of seam, and I think credit goes to Jaiswal for the catch that he took. It was an exceptional one. We have been putting in some effort on the field in practice, so I think it just paid off,” he mentioned.India had very little time to bowl before bad light stopped play. Manav Suthar then dismissed Prabath Jayasuriya for two with the final delivery of the day, leaving Sri Lanka at 8/2.Krishna stressed that creating chances is only half the job and the fielders also need to complete the opportunity.“100%. I think 50% of the job is bowling the ball there, getting an edge, but 50% is taking it as well, and we have been pretty good at doing that. I think it's also doing the simple things right, which we have been doing well, and that's what shows,” he added.Krishna also spoke about the need to adjust his length according to the pitch. He said the Indian coaching and analysis staff work together to decide the right approach for each surface.“Length is something that keeps changing with pitches that we play on. So we sit with analysts, coaches, and everything and decide on what's the kind of length that we want to be bowling on different surfaces. And yeah, natural length was something that I could say when I was not playing for the country, but when I'm here I need to be bowling every length that the team wants, and I'm trying to do that,” he concluded.
Article Summary: India bowler prasidh krishna believes aggression is best shown through his bowling. Krishna picked up a wicket with just his second delivery of the second over. Sri lanka were reduced to 8/2 before bad light ended day two. India had declared on 503/9 after centuries from devdutt padikkal and dhruv jurel.

Its sustainability efforts cover energy, waste, food packaging, community projects, education and opportunities for young people.As the championship reaches its season finale, the London E-Prix aims to show how electric racing can combine competition with efforts focused on sustainability and community impact.The London E-Prix will run on 100% certified renewable mains electricity, supported by solar power generated from Excel London’s eco-friendly extension. El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
